[2026-09-28 | AAPL | Underweight | -1.6% | -2.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL — trim, don't exit. Reduce roughly 45% of a benchmark-weight position (residual target ~55% of standard AAPL allocation, tighter than the plan's 60%): execute at least two-thirds now at 338.40 and via limit orders into 341.07–342.99, and time-limit the final slice to 5–8 sessions rather than leaving it contingent on a 345.34 push. No new money at 338.40. Work limit orders — not resting stops — through the compressed 335.96/334.30/330.33 cluster, accelerate the reduction on a close below 335.96 or 334.30, and take the final tactical exit on a close below 321.93 (50-SMA), with 309.90 the next reference. A daily close above 345.34 on ≥45M shares with the MACD histogram re-expanding invalidates the underweight but is not an automatic re-buy — restore toward neutral only on a held retest or after the Q4 print. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 release; do not score the call on five-day alpha.

**Investment Thesis**: DIRECTION IS SETTLED; SIZE AND EXECUTION ARE WHAT THE DEBATE CONTESTED, AND THAT IS WHERE I RULE. All seats — aggressive, conservative, neutral, Research Manager and trader — converge on reducing AAPL from 338.40; no seat defended full-weight at the wall. The disputed question is whether the residual is 60% (trader/aggressive), 50–55% (neutral) or 40–50% (conservative). I adopt the neutral construction hardened by the conservative seat's risk accounting.

The deciding evidence is geometry, and it is arithmetic rather than opinion. Resistance is stacked at 341.07 (09-25 highest close), 342.99 (09-28 high) and 345.34 (window high) — +0.9% / +1.4% / +2.1%. Support is at 335.96 (10-EMA), 334.30 (09-24 low), 330.33 (Bollinger mid) and 321.93 (50-SMA) — −0.7% / −1.2% / −2.4% / −4.9%, with the September higher-low at 309.90 another −8.4%. That is roughly 1:2.3 reward/risk against the 50-day before the 309.90 leg is counted. Nobody rebutted that arithmetic.

Three tape readings confirm buyer exhaustion is real. (1) Double-confirmed momentum divergence: price made a higher closing high at 341.07 on 09-25 while MACD printed 6.08 versus 9.61 at the 07-29 close of 338.19, and RSI fell from 71.65 (07-17) to 65.67 — two independent oscillators decelerating into supply. (2) Volume decay: the last 10 sessions average ~38.8M versus ~45.7M the prior 10 (−15%), with the 09-18 86.6M print stripped as third-Friday expiry noise; the final leg is on less participation. (3) Extension: +17.5% above a 200-SMA rising every session since June, with the 50–200 spread already 11.8% and the 50-day adding just 0.68% between 09-17 and 09-28.

The conservative seat wins the risk accounting and that is what moves my size. The aggressive seat's "2.1% risk on the trimmed third, 0.7% of a benchmark book" measures only the cost of being underweight if AAPL rallies; it ignores the residual. With the 330–336 ladder compressed into a 1.7% band, a decisive close below 330.33 slices the 10-EMA, the 334.30 swing low and the Bollinger mid simultaneously — close-based triggers will not fill where the chart says. Hence a residual of ~55% rather than 60%, a front-loaded reduction, limit orders rather than stops, and an explicit acceptance that the last 1–2% of sale price is not worth a gap through support.

Fundamentals are a gate, not a veto, and they are why this is Underweight rather than Sell. Against the trim: Q3 FY2026 revenue +16.4%, EPS $2.02 +28.7%, 9M EPS +22.4%, gross margin 50.06%, $62.2B net cash, a fully repaired July gap (first close back above 333.44 on 09-17), price 1.9% above a rising VWMA at 332.07, and 50 > 200 by 11.8% — that is not a short tape. For the trim: ~38.8x TTM EPS and ~35.7x EV/FCF already discount continued acceleration; nine-month FCF is flattered by a ~$14.6B favorable working-capital swing and a 28% capex cut; buybacks are down 12% YoY with the payout ratio at 72.9% of FCF; the $13.3B intangible build against a $13.5B noncurrent-liability increase has no footnote and implies future amortization; and the near-term news skew is negative — an unverified "$5.7B" Taction haptic-patent headline quantum, an escalated India CCPA iOS 18 probe, and foldable iPhone Duo demand skepticism at $1,999. Q4 FY2026 is unreported and lands in the same late-October window as this trim, so the trim is sized ahead of the event.

Where the seats overreach: the aggressive seat is wrong to dress a defensive trim as a "high-reward tactical strike," which encourages too much residual exposure; the conservative seat is right on gap realism (07-31's −7.36% on 132.5M shares proves only size controls risk, not stops) but overcorrects by requiring the full Q4 bar plus legal clarity before any re-engagement — legal clarity may take months, and a 40–50% residual risks unnecessary tracking error absent portfolio context.

Prior lessons are addressed, not ignored. This desk has repeatedly forfeited alpha underweighting AAPL inside intact uptrends (07-13, 07-20–07-24, 08-12–08-13, 08-17, 08-20–08-21, 08-24–08-28, and 09-08 at +5.9% five-day alpha; 09-15 still rose +2.5% raw). Three things distinguish this case: it is a trim into a five-level resistance stack at ~1:2.3 payoff, not a cut at support on momentum decay alone; the divergence is double-confirmed by volume decay into supply; and every independent seat plus the Research Manager and trader land on 45–50%, so this is corroboration rather than single-seat relabeling. The 09-15 reflection binds sizing explicitly: an invalidation gate just 2.1% above spot means this is a tactical trim that may revert to neutral within days, so I keep a real 55% core and pre-commit that a 345.34 breakout is not chased back — the core participates and only partial re-risk follows a held retest or Q4 confirmation. Per the 09-21 and 09-17 reflections, the evaluation gate is FQ4, a failed retest at 341–345, or a break of 321.93 — not five-day alpha.

What would change it: upgrade toward Hold/Overweight on a daily close above 345.34 on ≥45M shares with the MACD histogram re-expanding plus a held retest, or on Q4 EPS ≥$2.20, gross margin ≥49%, double-digit FY2027 guidance, buyback reacceleration, a credible explanation of the $13.3B intangible/$13.5B liability build, and legal/regulatory clarity. Downgrade toward Sell on a close below 321.93 and then 309.90, gross margin below 48% with decelerating revenue, an inventory write-down, or a quantified liability from the Taction verdict, the India CCPA action, or a foldable demand shortfall.

Stated gaps: no portfolio context, so all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation subject to their single-name limits; no options chain or implied volatility, so no collar or put spread into October can be priced and event risk must be managed through gross exposure; no segment/product/geographic/unit/ASP disclosure, so 50.06% margin durability is unattributable; no consensus forward EPS or peer set, so 38.8x/35.7x are mechanical and unverified and every cited level is technical, not valuation-derived; the "$5.7B" Taction quantum is a headline, not a measured liability; the cause of the 07-31 −7.36%/132.5M-share gap remains unestablished; and the tape figures are internally inconsistent across seats (38.8M/45.7M session averages versus an 86.6M 09-18 expiry print), which I resolve by treating 09-18 as noise and holding the 45M breakout gate.

**Price Target**: 328.0

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -2.8% (raw -1.6% against a rising SPY) is directionally consistent with the Underweight call, but this window is far too short to score a 1–3 month thesis that was explicitly gated on the late-October FQ4 print, the 321.93 break, or a failed 341–345 retest — none of which occurred. What it does support is the geometry argument: price failed to clear the 341.07–345.34 resistance stack and drifted lower, confirming buyer exhaustion at the wall, while the 345.34 invalidation gate and the fundamental concerns remain entirely untested. The concrete lesson is that the differentiator claimed against this desk's repeated underweighting losses inside intact uptrends — volume decay into a five-level resistance stack — is the part worth isolating and requiring as a precondition next time, rather than treating a single 5-day drift as vindication of a call whose real evidence lies a month out.

[2026-09-25 | AAPL | Underweight | -2.2% | -1.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL — trim into strength, do not exit. Cut roughly 40–45% of the current position across three slices (10–15% now or into any push toward 343; 20–25% on a limit at 345.30 inside the 343.00–346.20 zone; 10–15% on a daily close below the 10 EMA at 335.42 if that zone never prints), landing the core at ~55–60% of a standard allocation. No new money at 341.07, and the 349 level is a re-entry trigger, not a stop: only a daily close above 346.15 on ≥50M shares re-adds 15–20% of the original position. Hedge the retained core for gap risk (35–40% one-session gaps of −6.1% and −7.4% have printed inside three months) with 3–6 month puts or a collar funded above ~356, sized to cap the tail at 0.5–0.75% of total allocation; a daily close below the 50 SMA at 321.83 cuts to minimum weight and forces a full reassessment. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print.

**Investment Thesis**: DIRECTION OF THE ACTION IS A TRIM, NOT AN EXIT — and the decisive argument is the asymmetry the Research Manager and trader quantified and neither the aggressive nor the neutral analyst rebutted. At 341.07 AAPL sits 1.3% below the 345.34 (09-22 rejection high) / 346.15 (upper Bollinger) confluence, while the 50 SMA is 5.6% lower at 321.83 and the lower band 8.3% lower at 312.65. The base's measured move from the 300–322 range (342–344) is already delivered. On a simple de-rating to 28x FY27E EPS (~$10.10) from 33.8x, AAPL is $283 — ~17% downside with no earnings cut at all — against ~1.3% of first resistance. That is a valuation-derived penalty on the marginal share, and the aggressive analyst's answer (35x = $354, ~3.8% upside) argues for roughly one turn of expansion, which is the multiple being the risk rather than the edge. The confirmation failure is concrete and undisputed by all three seats: the record close came on 30.0M shares, ~74% of the 40.3M eleven-session average; the 09-22 push to 345.34 came on 40.7M versus 70.0M on the 09-10 range breakout; the MACD line at 6.211 sits far below its 9.609 July peak while price made a higher high and the histogram contracted four straight sessions (1.686 → 0.803). Full weight into an unconfirmed retest of known supply is the one genuinely uncompensated bet in this debate.

WHY UNDERWEIGHT AND NOT SELL. The aggressive analyst wins the structural half cleanly, and the neutral analyst's tape read is right: 341.07 closed at 99.8% of the session range above a rising 10 EMA (335.42), 50 SMA (321.83), 200 SMA (287.77) and VWMA (330.80), with an unbroken higher-low sequence (273.75 → 300.00 → 302.56 → 309.90 → 334.30), RSI 65.67 not overbought, ATR compressing at 2.05% of price, and 9M FY26 revenue +16.2% to $364.4B, operating income +21.7%, EPS +22.4%, gross margin 49.07% (50.06% in FQ3), 9M FCF $110.2B with CFO/NI at 1.15x and $62.2B net cash. Shorting into that stack is counter-trend and nobody proposed it. The trader's own framing — a partial staged sell down to a 60–65% core — is Underweight in substance, and Sell in this scale means exit; the evidence does not support exiting a franchise with accelerating earnings. Equally, the conservative analyst's 50–60% cut at market is not de-risking, it is a bearish directional call against an intact trend, and his "sell and be done" instruction plus a 321.83 review level 5.6% below spot pre-capitulates to a break that has not happened.

SIZING BETWEEN THE SEATS. I land at 40–45% trimmed / ~55–60% core — heavier than the aggressive's 35–40% because the valuation and volume evidence is decisive, lighter than the conservative's 50–60% because the trend, RSI and fundamentals are not. The neutral analyst's correction to the trader's construction is adopted because both colleagues' objections to it are valid: a 349 "stop" on sold shares is a disguised re-risk (the conservative is right on the label), so 349 becomes an explicit re-entry trigger requiring a daily close above 346.15 on ≥50M shares and only 15–20% of the original position, not the full trim. And the neutral analyst's point that a one-1% ATR hedge leg is not sized for a −7.4% gap is correct: on a 55–60% core a repeat of the 07-31 shock costs ~3.7% of total allocation, so the collar or 3–6 month puts must cap the tail at 0.5–0.75% of allocation, funded by upside above ~356, with slippage assumed through any stop.

THE DESK'S OWN RECORD IS PRICED IN, NOT IGNORED. The most damaging prior lesson is that AAPL Underweights inside intact uptrends have repeatedly forfeited five-day alpha (07-13, 07-20–07-24, 08-11–08-13, 08-17, 08-20–08-21, 08-24, 08-27–08-28, 09-02, 09-08 at −1.2%) while the 08-26, 09-04, 09-09, 09-10 and 09-11 overweights/holds paid +2.6% to +6.5%. Equally, the 09-14, 09-16 and 09-18 reflections all record the same execution error: tranches gated 2–3% below a rising tape never fill, and the plan earns no exposure to its own correct call. Both lessons are built into the structure: trim triggers include an immediate slice and a close-below-10-EMA slice so the reduction does not depend on 345.30 printing, and the rebuild side carries a time-based fallback — if neither the 329.40–330.80 zone nor a ≥50M-share close above 346.15 appears within roughly ten sessions while price holds the 10 EMA, re-add a small tranche at market rather than forfeiting participation. The 09-17 reflection's warning — don't state 3.7–5.1% downside targets unless price confirms them — is why the price target here is the 50 SMA at ~325 rather than the $283 de-rating extreme, which is held as a bear-case extension, not a base case.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT. Upgrade toward Overweight/Hold on a daily close above 345.34 and ideally above 346.15 on ≥50M shares (rebuild in tranches toward benchmark, targets 356.4 then 365), or on a Q4 print with gross margin ≥49.5%, inventory converting rather than writing down, and 10-Q reconciliation of the $12.1B intangibles and +32.6% other non-current liabilities. Downgrade toward Sell on a daily close below 321.83 that breaks the post-July structure, FQ4 gross margin below 48% (the Research Manager's own validation line), a revenue-growth deceleration below 10%, a step-up in the 17.58% tax rate toward a ~3% FY27 EPS headwind, or an inventory write-down that confirms the 94% build (+260% raw materials against −4% finished goods) was not a pre-ramp. Watch the monitoring sequence 334.30 → 329.40–330.80 → 321.83 → 312.65.

STATED GAPS. No portfolio context was supplied, so every size here is a fraction of the caller's own AAPL holding and standard benchmark weight, subject to their single-name and mega-cap limits. No options chain or implied-volatility data exists in this run, so the protective overlay cannot be priced — the hedge is directional guidance only. The fundamental inputs (FY26E EPS ~$9.05, FY27E ~$10.10, 37.7x/33.8x, gross margin, tax rate, inventory, intangibles) come from the research plan and were not independently verified against filings, and no FY27 consensus, segment, geographic or unit data is available to test margin durability. The "iPhone Duo," the Sept 23 event and the Ternus product cycle carry no pricing, ship dates or demand data and were correctly excluded from the sizing decision; the 09-23 event is unquantified and not modeled.

**Price Target**: 325.0

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The -1.9% five-day alpha (AAPL -2.2% vs. SPY) mildly favors the Underweight trim, but five sessions against a 1–3 month horizon is too short to judge the thesis — it validates the direction of the trim, not the 325 target. What it supports is the confirmation-failure argument: price stalled under the 345.34/346.15 confluence and rolled over instead of breaking out on ≥50M shares, which is precisely the uncompensated retest the plan refused to pay up for, and the ~2.2% decline likely put price through the 10 EMA at 335.42, meaning the fallback slice — not the 345.30 limit — did the work. The lesson for the next similar setup is to keep weighting execution toward the immediate and close-below-10-EMA tranches and treat the deep limit as optional, since the level that never prints is the one that never protects you.
